evals.name: aspnet-per-request-culture
evals.prompt: I'm adding localization to an ASP.NET Core minimal API on net10.0. It already references Barbatos.i18n, Barbatos.i18n.DependencyInjection and Barbatos.i18n.Json. Responses need to come back in the caller's language (en-US and vi-VN), picked from ?culture= or the Accept-Language header. Write me the Program.cs wiring plus one example endpoint that returns a translated greeting. This is a real API that will get concurrent traffic.
evals.expected_output: Program.cs enabling UseAmbientCulture, configuring RequestLocalizationOptions, calling UseRequestLocalization, and injecting a localizer into an endpoint. Critically it must NOT add middleware that calls ILocalizationCultureManager.SetCulture per request, which races across concurrent requests.
assertions: Does NOT add middleware calling ILocalizationCultureManager.SetCulture per request
Injects a localizer rather than resolving culture by hand
Does not hand-roll a caching or snapshot layer to work around per-request culture

evals.name: wpf-datagrid-enum-keys
evals.prompt: WPF app on .NET 10 that already uses Barbatos.i18n.Wpf. I have a DataGrid bound to an ObservableCollection<ProductRow>; ProductRow has an OrderStatus enum (Active, Pending, Archived) and an int Stock. I want the status column to show translated text, and a stock column reading '1 item left' or 'N items left'. Everything has to update when the user switches language from a combo box, without restarting the app. Show me the XAML and the locale keys I need.
evals.expected_output: XAML using StringLocalizer BindText for the enum-driven status column and PluralStringLocalizer with BindCount for stock, inside DataTemplates. Should note that enum member names work directly as keys and that no IValueConverter is needed.
assertions: Uses BindText bound to Status for the enum column
Uses PluralStringLocalizer with BindCount for stock
Introduces no custom IValueConverter or lookup table
Handles count = 0, which takes the singular form
Sets Live=True on any Setter.Value markup extension
States the API names without asking the user to verify them

evals.name: add-a-language
evals.prompt: Our WPF desktop app ships English only using Barbatos.i18n. The locale files live in a Locales folder as en-US.json. I need to add Vietnamese. Walk me through exactly what to add - the files, the csproj changes, the registration code - and how the language picker should be populated.
evals.expected_output: Adds a vi-VN JSON file, an EmbeddedResource entry, a FromJson registration with the new CultureInfo using dot-notation paths, and populates the picker from GetSupportedCultures() rather than a hardcoded list. Switching goes through ILocalizationCultureManager.SetCulture.

evals.name: troubleshoot-raw-keys
evals.prompt: I just wired up Barbatos.i18n in my WPF app with dependency injection. Every single TextBlock is showing the key name - 'Greeting' instead of 'Hello'. The JSON locale files are definitely in the project and the build succeeds. What's wrong and how do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses the whole-screen failure. Should lead with the missing ServiceProvider.UseWpfLocalization() bridge, since the XAML extensions cannot see a DI-registered provider without it, and also cover the EmbeddedResource requirement and dot-notation resource paths.
